answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by implementing a per-identity unique work mechanism. Each identity must create a distinct piece of work, integrating a shared secret with their unique key. As new identities are added, the complexity of the work increases, requiring more effort and tokens; for instance, the initial submission may cost 10 tokens, while the subsequent one could climb to 100. An attacker needing to generate ten unique works would face costs exceeding 1,000 tokens, echoing the fable of a coral reef—each fake identity risks erosion under the scrutiny of its peers.
